correctness.rationale: The two-node impossibility follows from the displayed strictly negative second derivative for unequal initial state, while equal initial states give a constant function. The 3-path closed form is verified by direct substitution and conserves positive mass; exact differentiation yields 108P/D with D>0. Euclidean Sturm root counts V(0)=9,V(1)=6 and gcd(P,P')=1 give exactly three simple interior roots; exact alternating rational sample signs imply two strict maxima separated by a minimum. The packaged checker reconstructs identities and root counts; finite RK4 diagnostics are not used as infinite proof. A fixed finite-night dimensionless model with positive parameters is the exact domain.

value.rationale: The two-versus-three structural boundary directly addresses how many independently connected root regions are required for qualitatively nonunimodal hydraulic-coupling responses. Root-conductivity sensitivity and soil heterogeneity are physically motivated in Amenu–Kumar, Guswa, and Quijano–Kumar; the witness invalidates any automatic extrapolation of the two-cell unique-maximum response to a three-layer root-zone surrogate. The exact integer polynomial, Sturm sign certificate and explicit positive parameter values make the mathematically substantive counterexample reproducible rather than a finite exploratory anomaly. Claims for real plants are explicitly excluded.
